newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA AVERAGE ONE-WEEK RATE UP TO 81 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA AVERAGE ONE-WEEK RATE UP TO 81 PCT.

text.p: The average rate on Romanian central bank one-week funds surged to 81 percent at this week's refinancing auction from 70.05 percent at the previous auction, central bank data showed on Friday.
A central bank (BNR) offer of 550 billion lei, down from 750 billion lei previously, was slightly oversubscribed, with two banks bidding a total 574.5 billion lei.
In a bid to slow down inflation and prop up the depreciating leu, the BNR has tightened its monetary policies, in line with International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommendations.
On Thursday, the BNR took another tough step, raising the minimum permitted rate on its one-week refinancing funds by 10 percentage points to 80 percent from 70 percent.
The move is expected to trigger rises in interbank money market rates, now trading at 67 percent for one-week funds.
The leu's interbank rate has slipped by some 45 percent to 5,950/980 against the dollar since January 1.
Year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent last December, almost three times the IMF-agreed 20 percent target for 1996.
An IMF mission is now in Bucharest discussing a new loan arrangement for Romania with the centrist coalition government which emerged from general elections last November.
IMF credits to Romania were suspended last year following upsets in the foreign exchange market and overspending by the former leftist government for election puposes.
